dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Annual rows reconcile exactly with the import log: May totals DLR-104 = 8 rows / $723.42, DLR-219 = 9 rows / $782.87; across all months 90 rows match on both sides to the cent"

"Zero duplication on every test: recharge_id and source_event_id are 100% unique across 24,542 rows; 0 content duplicates on (subscriber, date, amount, plan); import log duplicate_source_event_ids = 0, reconciliation_difference_usd = 0, all 41 files RECONCILED"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The flagged 31-May cluster is NOT duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect. It is simply the month-end batch-posting of legitimate annual-plan renewals by two West dealers (DLR-104 and DLR-219)"
"if the trend pack keys on posted_at rather than effective_event_date, the 31-May spike is a benign artifact of presentation, not substance"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "No region field exists in recharges.csv — \"West = DLR-104/DLR-219\" is inferred from the email and import log. A dealer master would independently confirm this mapping."
"The contract permitting monthly batch submission by these dealers is only asserted in Kavya's email, not provided as a document."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT reverse or hold the postings — they are reconciled, unique, and represent genuine revenue."

"Instead, re-plot the trend pack on effective_event_date (or tag batch-posted annual rows separately) and confirm the 31-May cosmetic spike flattens. Confirm the revenue recognition basis with Revenue Assurance."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The only actionable concern is a presentation issue — posting-date-based trend reports will show a cosmetic spike that disappears when keyed on effective_event_date."
"This is a reversible reporting adjustment, not a revenue correction."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The flagged 31-May cluster is NOT duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect" is more categorical than the evidence supports. The tests strongly reduce the duplicate-revenue and ingestion-defect hypotheses, but they do not by themselves rule out every form of reporting manipulation.

"No escalation is warranted" is reasonable for operational posting escalation if reconciliations hold, but it should be explicitly conditional on Revenue Assurance confirming the recognition basis and on the effective-date analysis.
"Annual amounts are approximately 12x the monthly plan price per plan ... — no inflation" uses price alignment as corroboration, not a sufficient test that amounts were not manipulated.
"they are ... genuine revenue" is stronger than the submission's own admission that the revenue-recognition basis remains unknown.
The claim that the cluster is specifically from West dealers remains dependent on the unverified dealer-to-region mapping and the email/import-log inference.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative handled is a benign posting-time artifact: legitimate annual-plan events occurred across 1–28 May but were uploaded or posted in a 31-May batch, creating a posting-date spike without duplicate cash or entitlement impact. The submission also acknowledges the remaining alternative that the pattern could distort revenue-recognition or downstream trend analytics if posted_at is used. It does not fully test the possibility of a reporting-definition or recognition-policy issue, however.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the conclusion explicitly conditional and provide a reproducible event-time reconciliation: join the 17 May 31-May postings to unique source_event_ids and cash/entitlement records, show their effective dates and amounts, then obtain Revenue Assurance confirmation of the recognition basis before stating that no escalation is warranted.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell to index 59 in June while control regions held flat (~100)" — sourced to "tickets.csv".

"464–1,094 NOVA sessions ended failed/abandoned with no case created (382 pre-auth in June alone); 411 distinct subscribers affected, ~175 never recovered in any subsequent session" — sourced to "ivr_interactions.jsonl".

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The drop is primarily a measurement and authentication artifact — with a genuine but smaller self-service component."
"Transfers are the route to agents and cases; their collapse from 49.5% to 3.3% alongside tripled pre-auth deaths is deflection, not resolution."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "CAUSAL CLAIMS (tentative): Authentication/prompt defects combined with a case-exclusion rule cause a significant part of the case drop".
"UNKNOWNS: 7-day repeat-contact/callback rate; exact containment metric denominator definition; what operationally happens to a subscriber whose session fails at authentication."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT expand nationally. Keep the South pilot running (reversible)."

"Reconcile IVR sessions to CareDesk cases so nothing is invisible. Fix the known auth/prompt defects. Re-evaluate over at least two complete weeks against an E/N/W control before any rollout decision."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Add pre-auth abandonment and all-contact containment to the dashboard."
"Can you provide the repeat-contact data: of South subscribers who hit an authentication error, how many contacted us again within 48–72 hours on any channel?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The drop is primarily a measurement and authentication artifact" is directionally plausible but not quantitatively established; the submission does not show how much of the decline is attributable to missing case creation versus genuine resolution.
"The tripled pre-auth failures are would-be complaints" overstates what abandonment establishes. They may represent friction or failed journeys, but not all abandoned sessions are complaints.
"new self-service stages ... cause a genuine minority of the improvement" is not demonstrated by stage presence or usage alone; linked journey outcomes are needed.
"Transfers are the route to agents and cases" and the conclusion that their decline is "deflection, not resolution" may be too categorical without tracing transfer, case, and resolution outcomes.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the possibility that some improvement was genuine by identifying new self-service stages and preserving a "genuine but smaller self-service component." However, it missed a fully developed benign interpretation of some pre-auth abandonment—for example, authentication failures that were retried successfully or represented non-complaint interactions—and did not validate this with sampled call listening or linked subscriber journeys.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Directly link IVR sessions to downstream cases, repeat contacts, callbacks, and resolutions, supplemented by sampled listening to abandoned calls, before labeling abandonment as unrecorded complaints or estimating the genuine self-service contribution.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies inverter_events.csv and gives specific observations: four events from 27 May–4 Jun, four distinct inverter IDs, impact_mw = 0, cleared = yes, severity, and duration range.

The wording distinguishes uncertainty about export completeness and impact_mw population from observed row values: "Completeness is the only genuine question" and "a uniformly-zero column can also mean the field is not actively populated."

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks event wording against impact_mw, cleared, severity, duration, and recurrence rather than treating names as proof of failure.

It tests two plausible innocent/data-quality explanations: an incomplete export and a defaulted impact_mw field. The analysis is primarily based on one event-log source rather than independent operational channels, so it does not reach the highest anchor.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly says completeness "cannot be confirmed from this export alone" and recommends a cheap, decision-changing check rather than escalation.
It appropriately qualifies the zero-impact interpretation by noting that impact_mw may not be actively populated, while still stating what the file does and does not show.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Do not escalate" follows from the observed zero impact, cleared status, low severities, short durations, and lack of recurrence.

The proposed next action—confirming the date-range filter and plant-wide event count, plus checking whether impact_mw is computed rather than defaulted—is low-cost and discriminating, while preserving the option to stop if the export is complete.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion is accurately scoped: "nothing in this file shows measurable impact, recurrence, or any open fault condition" rather than claiming that no underlying issue is possible.
It matches the evidence-supported stopping point and does not invent a plant problem from the seven-minute warning or event names.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The exam explicitly instructs not to infer equipment failure or commercial impact from event names" is a reference to instructions rather than evidence; the rejection is nevertheless independently supported by the event fields.
"For a multi-inverter plant, that is thin" is a reasonable characterization but is not itself a measured finding and depends on plant scope/context outside the event rows.

"No open fault condition" is slightly broader than the evidence: cleared = yes establishes that the listed events are closed, not that every possible plant fault is absent. The surrounding wording limits the claim to what is shown in this file.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The four rows may be an incomplete or filtered export, or impact_mw may be a defaulted/unpopulated field. Either explanation could make the apparent benign result unreliable, so export scope and field-population checks are the appropriate alternatives to test before fully closing the matter.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Prioritize one explicit validation of export completeness: verify the applied date range and plant-wide event count for that same window, then use the result to decide whether the zero-impact/cleared pattern is representative.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Recomputing from dispatch_blocks.csv reproduces both numbers exactly"
"base_schedule_mw is the pre-pilot QCA schedule"
Evidence Table cites dispatch_blocks.csv, AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md, and DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf for the principal numerical and mechanism claims.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: "31.6% is a cross-day comparison — 29 May (AI-assisted) versus 28 May (conventional)"
"28 May happens to be the single highest-penalty day in the entire 8-day file"
The submission cross-checks penalty, generation-gap, firmware, weather, schedule revisions, penalty bands, and the concentration of penalties in STOW blocks.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Still causally unidentified: the effect's generality across typical high-wind days (only one pilot day exists)"
"whether the revision was ex-ante forecast skill or hindsight adjustment"
"Net value (energy minus penalty) is not computed."

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Keep the pilot running"
"Run the AI schedule with its base-schedule shadow over several high-wind stow days"
The recommendation preserves the observed potential benefit while requiring replication, firmware control, ex-ante timing verification, and net-value measurement before scale-up.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "the defensible effect is about 17.5% on one weather-matched day — roughly half the advertised 31.6%"
"report the ~17.5% within-day figure, NOT ‘31.6%’"
The conclusion distinguishes the arithmetic correctness of the headline from its weakness as a controlled causal estimate, while retaining a smaller observed/mechanical benefit.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the within-day effect (~17.5%) is identifiable" is somewhat too strong: the calculation identifies the mechanical penalty difference between two schedules holding realized generation fixed, but does not by itself establish the causal effect of the AI pilot or its ex-ante forecast skill.

Calling the counterfactual "clean" and "no-pilot" assumes base_schedule_mw is a valid pre-pilot alternative and that the schedule revision was not informed by information unavailable under the base process; the submission appropriately flags this timing issue but could state the limitation more prominently.
"The mechanism ... is plausible" is reasonable, but the evidence does not establish that schedule lowering rather than other contemporaneous factors would generalize beyond this single pilot day.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% figure is a correctly calculated but non-controlled cross-day association, while the 17.5% result is best described as a same-day schedule-substitution or mechanical penalty reduction—not yet a general causal estimate of AI performance. The pilot may still have commercial value, but lower penalties could be offset by forgone energy revenue and the result may not replicate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run several pre-specified high-wind days with the AI schedule and a contemporaneous base-schedule shadow, verify revision timestamps precede realized generation, hold firmware constant where feasible, and compare net commercial value rather than penalty alone.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the primary conclusion to named sources: "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx (Swiss Matrix)" and "product_master_current.xlsx (Read Me)."
It identifies specific fields and context, including "90211000," "90211090," "P1001," the "2025-11-04 entry date," and the Read Me qualification "not customs-ruling status."

However, it does not provide exact worksheet names, row numbers, quoted matrix entries, or the comparator event/log supporting the assertion that it flagged the value "solely" because of the code difference.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly tests alternatives: "'90211000 is a keying error for 90211090.' Rejected" and "'Helios is the source of truth, so the declaration must conform to it.' Rejected."
It also tests the hypothesis that "A mismatch flag means a declaration error" and connects the rejection to missing code-system and version fields.

The reasoning is somewhat overconfident in treating shared HS6 "902110" as establishing that "there is no mismatch where classification is actually harmonised"; shared HS6 does not by itself validate the complete national classification or declaration.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table labels the main source-supported claims "High" confidence and identifies concrete missing evidence: "A code-system identifier and nomenclature version stamped on each code."

The decision is appropriately non-escalatory for the benign mismatch pattern, but statements such as "exactly the code" and "proving codes are date- and jurisdiction-dependent" are stronger than the summarized evidence warrants.

The submission also claims the comparator "structurally cannot distinguish a real misclassification from a cross-system difference," but this would ideally be supported by the actual schema fields and comparator logic rather than the schema description alone.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the mechanism as "a cross-code-system false positive generated by a comparator that has no concept of code-system or effective-date differences."

It distinguishes "the eight-digit Helios commercial commodity code" from the Swiss tariff code and EU CN8, and notes that the product master labels the Helios value "migration-mapped" and "not customs-ruling status."
It correctly identifies effective dating and jurisdiction as relevant lineage dimensions, citing the EU change from "90211010 to 90211090 at 2025-07-01."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommendation "Do NOT escalate this as a likely declaration error" is proportionate to the documented Swiss-versus-Helios code-system mismatch and avoids an unsupported compliance escalation.

The proposed decision is not fully operationalized: it does not specify a reversible control such as documenting the false-positive disposition, manually confirming the dated Swiss entry, or updating the comparator to carry jurisdiction, nomenclature version, and effective date.
The missing-evidence section points toward safer remediation but is truncated after "The effective-dated Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001 (both the".

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The automated tool flagged it solely because it differs from 'Helios 90211090'" is not directly supported by a cited comparator log or event record.

"At the internationally harmonised six-digit level, both codes share HS6 902110 — there is no mismatch where classification is actually harmonised" overstates what shared HS6 establishes; it supports alignment at HS6, not necessarily correctness of every national tariff digit.

"The EU code for P1001 itself changed from 90211010 to 90211090 at 2025-07-01, proving codes are date- and jurisdiction-dependent" uses a single change as proof of a broader proposition without quoting the underlying rows or clarifying whether the change was a nomenclature revision, product remapping, or other event.

"The comparator ... structurally cannot distinguish a real misclassification from a cross-system difference" is plausible from the schema description but should be demonstrated against the actual comparator implementation or alert logic.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The alert could still reflect a genuine classification or data-lineage issue if 90211000 is not the applicable Swiss code for the specific P1001 transaction, if the matrix entry was not effective on 2025-11-04, or if the comparator used an intended normalized code that was incorrectly populated. A dated Swiss tariff row or binding classification record and the comparator's actual comparison inputs would resolve this; the submission identifies some of this missing evidence but does not complete the verification.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote the exact Swiss Matrix and product-master rows, the effective-date and jurisdiction fields, and the comparator alert inputs/log, then recommend recording the alert as a documented false positive while adding code-system, nomenclature-version, jurisdiction, and effective-date fields to the comparison.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Preference = Yes claimed for P1006, but no supplier support linked in ClearView" — citing declaration.pdf and review_note.txt.
"SUP-02/P1006 (Ireland) is Expired: valid_to 2025-07-31... entry dated 2025-09-18" — citing supplier_origin_register.csv and supplier_declaration_reference.txt.
"Register absence ‘does not prove no document exists outside the register’" — citing supplier_declaration_reference.txt and origin-workshop.md.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference = Yes on the form means the claim is supported.’ Rejected: the indicator is a claim, not evidence."
"‘ERP/Helios shows US origin, so the claim is simply false — reject it.’ Rejected as too strong" because Helios was "‘never designed to prove preference.’"
"‘SUP-02's Irish declaration covers it.’ Rejected: the declaration expired 2025-07-31... before the 2025-09-18 entry date."
"‘The shipping route to Ireland or the 0% duty rate settles the origin question.’ Rejected: logistics and duty rate do not establish preferential origin."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Crucially, this is ‘not established,’ not ‘proven false.’"
"The register itself states that its silence ‘does not prove that no document exists outside the register’" and the workshop notes confirm the register is "‘not always updated.’"
"do not raise a fraud or error escalation on a register gap alone."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "ERP/Helios origin is US; Helios was ‘never designed to prove preference’ — it carries manufacturing country, not origin proof."
"Which supplier actually sourced this particular shipment... the packet never identifies the sourcing supplier."
"‘Use ERP where blank’ is for extraction testing, ‘not for clearing a preference claim’; schema does not model origin-evidence type."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim and treat the line as non-preferential (MFN) for now" — a proportionate interim control, particularly because the line is "duty-neutral here (0.0%)."
"Request... the current supplier declaration for the actual sourcing supplier... plus the rule invoked."
"Escalate to a formal error or fraud referral only if that verification is requested and no valid proof is produced — not on the register gap alone."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "An expired document cannot support a current preference claim" is stated categorically; the submission does not establish the applicable agreement's rules for retrospective coverage, document validity, or whether another valid document supersedes it.

"Other suppliers... hold current, valid EU-origin declarations" is treated as established from register status, but the submission appropriately notes that none is linked to this shipment and does not show the declarations' precise scope or rule.

"Treat the line as non-preferential (MFN) for now" is operationally safe as a hold/no-preference disposition, but could be misread as a final origin determination before the actual supplier and governing preference rule are verified.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The claim could still be valid if the shipment was sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05, SUP-06, or another EU supplier and a current declaration exists outside the incomplete register. Helios's US manufacturing-country data does not disprove preferential originating status, and the absence of a ClearView link does not prove that the required evidence does not exist.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and trace the actual shipment's sourcing supplier, the applicable preference agreement and origin rule, and the complete supplier declaration or supporting origin proof before converting the interim hold into a final non-preferential determination.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185/262 (70.6%) qcore_release_ts values are stamped at exactly 02:10:00" and "42 HOLD rows have null qcore_release_ts" — specific counts and fields are traceable to named files.

"Excluding 02:10 rows drops median evidence-to-release from 21.3 h to 8.4 h" — provides a reproducible comparison, but the semantic interpretation of the timestamp is not established by the cited extracts.

"HOLD represents the entire most recent week — $5.97M inventory / $6.64M shortage exposure censored" — usefully identifies selection and right-censoring risk, though the source alignment issue is only briefly acknowledged.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "QCore records the release date but defaults the time to its batch boundary, so the intraday duration is fabricated" — this is a causal conclusion not demonstrated by the extract; the relevant alternative is that the timestamp is an interface commit rather than a decision time.
"The genuine process is fast, and the slow headline is an artifact" — overstates what can be inferred after excluding 70% of observations and retaining only 23 routine rows.

"Survivorship: All 42 open-HOLD batches... have no release timestamp" — correctly identifies a separate mechanism that can bias observed cycle time, but the submission does not fully separate workflow delay from interface-timing effects.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The table labels several findings "High" confidence even though the meaning of qcore_release_ts is the decisive unresolved issue.
"likely CertVault nightly-index lag, not a control failure" and "would need a live-portal check" appropriately preserve uncertainty for the COA hypothesis.

"What Would Change the Decision" identifies the timestamp definition and aligned extract as decision-relevant missing evidence, but the headline conclusion remains more certain than those gaps permit.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "the apparent cycle time should NOT be shipped as a KPI yet" — a safe and useful decision reframing that prevents optimizing a potentially invalid measure.
"Smallest verification: Pull the true disposition timestamp from live QCore for 5–10 batches" — proposes a small, reversible test with a clear interpretation.
The recommendation to define endpoints and obtain a source-aligned extract is useful, but calling the residual 5.5-hour result the "genuine process" could lead to premature performance conclusions.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects "1.5 days is a real, trustworthy cycle time" using the SOP clock, timestamp concentration, and backlog censoring.
It rejects "The data is broken — throw it out" and preserves a verification path, which is a useful alternative test.

The COA hypothesis is described as "more consistent with CertVault's nightly index lag," but that explanation is not independently tested and the strongest competing explanation—actual release before certificate availability—is not fully bounded.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Pull the true disposition timestamp from live QCore for 5–10 batches whose extract time is 02:10:00" — highly targeted evidence that directly discriminates default/interface timing from real event timing.
"The data-catalog definition of qcore_release_ts" is correctly identified as the decisive definitional question.
The request for "a fresher, source-aligned extract" addresses temporal inconsistency and prevents overconfident joins across LabTrack and QCore snapshots.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "QCore records the release date but defaults the time to its batch boundary" is asserted from the 02:10 concentration and source freshness, but those facts do not prove defaulting rather than an interface-commit convention.

"The genuine process is fast" and "the slow headline is an artifact" overstate the evidence after excluding most rows and selecting only 23 routine observations; the residual result may still mix workflow and interface timing.
Treating the 02:10 rows as an "artifact" and the remaining rows as valid is not justified until event/decision timestamp semantics or an event log is obtained.
"COA MISSING" being likely CertVault indexing lag is plausible but not demonstrated by the supplied evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 value may be a genuine enterprise interface-commit timestamp rather than a fabricated or defaulted decision time. Apparent cycle time could therefore combine real workflow delay with delayed or batched interface publication; neither the 45.5-hour receipt clock nor the 5.5-hour filtered result is safe as a KPI without event/decision timestamp semantics and source-aligned data.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain the qcore_release_ts data-catalog definition and a small event-level extract for the same 5–10 02:10 batches, including evidence-available, decision/disposition, and interface-commit timestamps from a coherent snapshot. Use it to determine whether the KPI measures workflow time, publication latency, or both before reporting any filtered cycle-time result.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "24 open buys = $166,496 (qty x unit quote)"; "part_requests.csv (recomputed)"
"HA-0022 belt on-hand 3 but available -1" supported by "spare_parts.csv + maintenance_email.txt"
"Global stock view (MaintStar-global) dated 2026-06-26" supported by "source_freshness.csv"

The submission identifies relevant files, fields, and policy gates, and triangulates requests, stock, restrictions, email, and freshness. However, the 8/12/4 classification is not fully reconciled to the detailed candidate rows and the evidence does not show row-level support for every request.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The new global search is a lead generator, not a transfer approver"
"'The search found a match, so transfer it.' Rejected" using part number, revision, qualification, and unreserved-stock gates
"'available_qty_global = -1 means there is no stock.' Rejected" using on-hand quantities and Leon's warning

The reasoning separates semantic matching from operational transferability and tests several plausible explanations. It does not fully model how stale global data affects the supposedly actionable population or distinguish transfer eligibility from actual PO-cancellation economics.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Global stock view ... dated 2026-06-26, refreshed monthly" and "local CMMS screens are live"
"only 8 of 24 clear all four gates"
"The honest firm saving is ~$20.5k"

The submission recognizes stale data and labels 12 cases as needing checks, but it still states that 8 requests are transfer-ready right now and calls the saving firm despite relying partly on an approximately four-week-old global snapshot and without validating live reservations, PO cancellation costs, or timing.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "The new global search is a lead generator, not a transfer approver"
"Return the 12 needs-check requests to the planner, each with the specific question it needs answered"
"Raise cross-site transfers for the 8 actionable requests and cancel those external POs today"

The reframing is useful and gives a practical triage structure, but the instruction to raise transfers and cancel external POs today is too aggressive given stale inventory data and unverified live availability. A safer reversible pilot would require current-site confirmation and transfer/PO cancellation controls before commitment.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "'Same part family = interchangeable.' Rejected" based on revision and SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK constraints
"'A matching text description is enough.' Rejected" based on blank manufacturer part numbers
"'Pull the reserved servo drives from the other plants.' Rejected" based on safety-critical reservations and Engineering's decline

The submission actively rejects multiple plausible but unsafe interpretations and gives evidence for each. It could more explicitly state what evidence would revive the conclusion that some currently actionable matches are not safe because of stale inventory or local reservations.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live availability for HA-0022 (belt) and ME-0006 (seal)"
"An Engineering interchangeability sign-off for VLV-3722 rev A vs rev B"
"receiving-site qualification confirmation for the SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK rows"

The requested evidence is specific and decision-linked rather than a generic request for more data. The highest-priority query should have been an immediate live inventory/reservation reconciliation for all eight proposed transfers, not only the negative-availability cases.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Only 8 of 24 clear all four gates" and "8 ... transfer-ready right now" overstate certainty because the global MaintStar availability snapshot is stale and local reservation status is not shown as freshly confirmed for all eight.

"Raise cross-site transfers for the 8 actionable requests and cancel those external POs today" is not adequately supported and may create operational or financial risk before live stock, reservation, receipt, and cancellation status are confirmed.

"The honest firm saving is ~$20.5k" treats candidate avoided purchase value as firm savings without evidence on transfer cost, PO cancellation terms, timing, or whether any external orders are already committed.

The submission should reconcile the detailed match-row counts with the stated 8 actionable, 12 needs-check, and 4 non-transferable totals, especially where grouped requests and blank-part-number requests overlap.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic matches may be valid candidate equivalents, but the apparently actionable $20.5k could shrink materially after live local reservation checks, refreshed inventory, receiving-site qualification, and confirmation that external POs can actually be cancelled. The safer interpretation is candidate value rather than firm savings until those controls are completed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a live, timestamped reconciliation for every proposed transfer—manufacturer part number and revision, receiving-site qualification, unreserved quantity, reservation/criticality, and external-PO cancellation status—then authorize only a small reversible transfer pilot before cancelling purchases.
